item.title: CAFA urges unified policies to grow Africa’s fashion economy to $500bn
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The Confederation of African Fashion,CAFA, has called on African countries to harmonise their fashion policies, strengthen intellectual property protection and invest in local manufacturing as part of efforts to grow the continent’s fashion economy to $500 billion. The President of CAFA, Professor Lai Labode, made the call during the unveiling of the joint stand of the organisation and the Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy at the ongoing CANEX WKND 2026. Labode said Africa had no shortage of creative talent but lacked the structures and policies needed to translate its creative potential into economic value. “In Africa, we don’t have a shortage of talent. What Africa needs is structure. Money always follows structure,” he said. He said the African Fashion Industry Growth Charter, developed by CAFA, was built around 10 pillars designed to address challenges across the fashion value chain, including policy harmonisation, raw material cultivation and processing, intellectual property protection, counterfeiting, logistics and market access. Labode stressed the need for African countries to process their raw materials locally instead of exporting them in largely unprocessed forms, arguing that local value addition would create jobs and retain more wealth within the continent. Using cotton production as an example, he compared Brazil’s reported $5.3 billion cotton exports with China’s earnings from cotton production and processing, saying Africa needed to build its own processing capacity to compete more effectively. He also identified intellectual property protection as a major priority, noting that African designers and creative businesses needed stronger systems to protect their original works from counterfeiting and unauthorised use. On market access, Labode disclosed plans to establish about 10 African fashion houses across the continent, alongside outlets in New York, Paris, Milan and London, to promote African designers and connect them with international markets. He called for common intellectual property rules and standards across African countries, warning that fragmented systems could weaken the continent’s competitiveness. The CAFA president also urged member states to support the intellectual property framework under the African Continental Free Trade Area, saying the relevant protocol annexes had been passed in February 2026 but required wider participation by African countries. Speaking in the same vein, the Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, identified private-sector partnerships, policy development and infrastructure as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s fashion industry. Musawa said the collaboration with CAFA should translate into tangible economic benefits, particularly job creation, while promoting African unity, cultural pride and soft power. item.title: CANEX WKND 2026 lights up Lagos as Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour headline star-studded concert tonight
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku & Tony-Okafor Favour The 2026 edition of Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, CANEX WKND, which opened at the Professor Wole Soyinka Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos on Thursday, continues this evening with a blockbuster concert. Headlining the night are some of Africa’s biggest music stars, including Nigeria’s Davido, Congolese sensation Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Cali-Ber Tha Grime, Sabrina Francis and Nigerian DJ duo Wanni X Handi. The concert will bring together performers from Africa and the Caribbean for an evening of live music, rhythm and cultural celebration. The four-day gathering, themed “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World”, has brought the once moribund Arts Theatre back to life. It convened leading voices from film, music, fashion, sport, publishing, gastronomy and business to advance trade, investment and commercial opportunities across Africa’s creative economy. The opening day featured a series of masterclasses and sessions, including Building Your Brand as an Independent Artist, Podcasting for Success, Fashion Masterclass: Building Profitable Fashion Brands, and Building Sustainable Business Models in the Performing Arts. In attendance were Vice-President Kassim Shettima, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Afreximbank President and Chairman of the Board of Directors, Dr George Elombi; Nigeria’s Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; and African Continental Free Trade Area Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene. Other dignitaries included the Minister of Arts, Culture, Tourism, and the Creative Economy for Nigeria, Hon Hannatu Musa Musawa; Mrs Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President of Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank; Hon Ginger Moxey, Minister for Grand Bahama; Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba; filmmaker Funke Akindele; and actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu among other dignitaries. Speaking while declaring the programme open, Shettima said the world will eventually hear about the can-do spirit of African women. He commended Afreximbank for committing $2 billion to Africa’s creative industries by 2027, noting that the industry is not just about entertainment, but also serious economic infrastructure. Shettima took the audience down memory lane, recalling almost 50 years ago when the same Arts Theatre hosted the second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture, FESTAC ’77, where the Black World declared through music, dance, literature and art that “our culture was not just a footnote to history, but the very core within it. “In 1977, we came to celebrate our culture. In 2024, we are here to capitalize it,” he said. He urged Africans to be proud of who they are without asking for anything in return. item.title: Bimbo Ademoye shines in dual roles
item.description: By Ammah Sarah Bimbo Ademoye is stepping into one of the biggest moments of her career as she takes on a dual role in the highly anticipated film,”The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives.” The actress is not only starring in the film, she is also serving as an Executive Producer, a move that shows her growth from screen star to power player behind the scenes. In the film, Ademoye plays the character Iya Femi, a role fans are already excited to see her bring to life. Sharing the news with her followers, Ademoye expressed her excitement about being part of the production, describing it as a special experience from start to finish. The film has already started making waves internationally. From Toronto to London, it has enjoyed screenings at two prestigious Oscar-qualifying film festivals, earning attention from global audiences and critics. Now, the excitement is moving to Africa. The film is set to celebrate its premiere in Africa November 29, an event fans across the continent have been waiting for. After the premiere, it will be released in Nigeria and other West African countries on December 4, and in the UK, USA, and Canada on December 11. item.title: Toke Makinwa takes fans down memory lane with live podcast
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Still basking in the glow of her surprise 32nd birthday party, Toke Makinwa is taking her fans on a nostalgic trip back to where it all began. The Nigerian media personality and actress has announced plans to stage a live podcast of the first episode of her live show on November 21 in Lagos. Taking to Instagram to share the news, the former OAP wrote: “A little nostalgic trip down memory lane… We have come so far. I remember my very first episode. Let’s meet, let’s connect, November 21, in Lagos.” Her birthday on November 3 was anything but quiet. Friends and well-wishers pulled off a surprise party for the queen, and videos from the celebration showed her enjoying every moment with her circle. Though she admitted she wasn’t easily surprised, this time she dofed her cap for her friends. “I had the longest birthday blues, did not want to do anything on my birthday which is not like me and I am so thankful my circle did not listen,” she wrote. “She had two outfits and when everyone kept cancelling from coming to my house, I agreed to go to dinner at @maisonprivelagos. “I walked in totally surprised. I had the best dinner.” The post Toke Makinwa takes fans down memory lane with live podcast appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebonyi Youths Protest Political Violence, Intimidation Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: Hundreds of youths in Ebonyi State have staged a peaceful march through Abakaliki, the state capital, calling for an end to political violence, intimidation and harassment of opposition members ahead of the 2027 general elections. The protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Ebonyi Youth for Democracy, said they came from the 13 local government areas of the state to demand a peaceful political atmosphere in which all citizens can participate without fear. The demonstrators marched through major streets in Abakaliki, displaying placards with messages including, “Democracy Needs Peaceful Ideas, Not Weapons” and “Protect Freedom of Speech in Ebonyi.” Addressing journalists during the rally, a spokesperson for the group said the youths would not accept any attempt to undermine their constitutional rights. “Our constitutional rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly are not negotiable,” the spokesperson said. The group also expressed concern over reported incidents of physical violence, harassment and voter intimidation targeting opposition figures in parts of the state. “We will not sit by while political thuggery and intimidation threaten to ruin our state’s democratic process. Every citizen, regardless of party alignment, deserves to participate without fear for their safety,” the spokesperson added. The protesters called on security agencies and state institutions to intervene and ensure a level playing field for all political parties. Another youth coordinator said opposition parties should be able to campaign, present their programmes and engage voters without threats or intimidation. “Opposition parties must be allowed to campaign safely, present their platforms, and engage with voters without constant threat of violence,” the coordinator said. The group said the march was part of efforts by young people in the state to demand accountability and promote peaceful political participation as the 2027 general elections approach. item.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
item.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Pediatrician Adam Ratner, who specializes in infectious disease, told AFP such deaths are “tragic, and that is completely preventable.” Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. “Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said. “The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions.” Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year across the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. item.title: Naira appreciates to N1,375/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira today appreciated to N1,375 per dollar from N1,380 in the parallel market on Thursday. Similarly, the naira appreciated to N1,349 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the official market fell to N1349 per dollar from N1350.45 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N1.45 appreciation for the naira. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N29 per dollar from N29.55 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM rose by 130.8 percent to $232.9 billion from $100.9 billion on Thursday. item.title: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff after midterm losses
item.description: US President Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration policies, as his new chief of staff following the Republican Party’s losses in the midterm elections. Miller, who served as deputy chief of staff and senior adviser during Trump’s first administration, will replace Susie Wiles, who resigned after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. Trump announced that Wiles would move to the “Trump Political Operation”, praising her for what he described as an outstanding performance as chief of staff. Miller, one of Trump’s closest and most loyal aides, is expected to assume the new position on Monday. He remained firmly behind Trump following his defeat in the 2020 presidential election and returned with him to the White House last year. Wiles submitted her resignation to Trump on Thursday night, according to a US official who spoke to CBS News, the BBC’s media partner. Three sources also told CBS that her departure was connected to the Republican Party’s midterm election losses. In a statement, Wiles described her time in Trump’s administration as “the honor of a lifetime”. “I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” she said. “While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will.” It remained unclear whether her deputies would retain their positions at the White House. Wiles, 69, was regarded as one of the most influential figures in the Trump administration and a close confidante of the president. As recently as last month, Trump dismissed suggestions that she could soon leave her position, declaring that there was “zero chance” of her replacement. “Susie is here and she’s gonna be here for a long time,” he had said. Wiles announced in September that she was in remission, six months after being diagnosed with cancer. Her departure is not the only high-profile exit from the Trump administration following the midterm elections, which have triggered fresh debate within the Republican Party over how to respond to voters’ rejection of its agenda. Several Justice Department officials have also resigned, including John Eisenberg, head of the department’s National Security Division, and Jason Reding Quiñones, who was involved in investigations concerning officials who examined Trump’s handling of classified documents. Meanwhile, Democrats criticised Trump’s appointment of Miller, accusing the president of maintaining the same policies despite the electoral setback. Democratic Congressman Robert Garcia, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee when Democrats assume control of the chamber, said he would continue investigating Miller and what he described as his misconduct. “Just days after the American people rejected his corrupt and lawless presidency, Donald Trump is doubling down. item.title: Troops arrest notorious terrorist, hit Dogo Gide’s hideouts in Zamfara forest
item.description: Troops of the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, have arrested a suspected notorious terrorist in the Kagarko Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The troops also intensified clearance operations against terrorists and dismantled several hideouts in Zamfara, as part of efforts to rid the region of criminal elements. The Acting Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Capt. Tamuno Sinivie, disclosed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna on Friday. Sinivie said troops of Sector 1, in collaboration with operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), arrested the suspect, identified as Auta Maikyala, during an intelligence-led operation on Nov. 5. He said the suspect was apprehended at a hospital in Kagarko town, where he had reportedly gone for medical attention over a gunshot wound sustained during an encounter with a rival faction. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect was allegedly involved in several attacks on communities, kidnapping, and cattle rustling. He added that the suspect was currently in custody for further investigation and prosecution. Sinivie further said that troops conducted clearance operations at Aljummu Hausa, Aljummu Fulani, and Tunga Magaji villages in the Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara on the same day. The acting media information officer said the operations led to the clearance of several terrorist hideouts, thereby restricting the activities of criminal elements and enhancing security in the affected communities. He also disclosed that the air component of the Nigerian Air Force conducted air interdiction operations against identified terrorist locations in Babban Doka and Kuyumbana Forest in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara. Sinivie said the locations were suspected to be associated with a wanted terrorist kingpin, Dogo Gide. According to him, the air operations followed credible intelligence that terrorists were assembling in the area to plan and coordinate criminal activities. The acting media information officer added that troops were currently maintaining dominance over the general area. Sinivie reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to sustaining its operational tempo to protect lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. He urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information on suspected terrorists and their activities to support security agencies in tackling criminal threats. (NAN) The post Troops arrest notorious terrorist, hit Dogo Gide’s hideouts in Zamfara forest appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Malami condemns alleged attacks on ADC campaign
item.description: Former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, has condemned alleged attacks and acts of intimidation against members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. Malami, the ADC governorship candidate in Kebbi State, also expressed appreciation to residents for what he described as the massive turnout and support for former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the party’s leadership at the campaign event held on Thursday, November 5. In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Assistant on Media, Mohammed Bello Doka, Malami said the turnout demonstrated the people’s determination to pursue a better future for the state and the country. He commended Atiku for his leadership and commitment to national renewal, while acknowledging the contributions of the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, other party leaders, campaign coordinators, supporters and volunteers. Malami said the party was committed to building a Nigeria that was affordable and secure, identifying rising fuel costs, insecurity and unemployment as issues requiring urgent attention. He also outlined his priorities for Kebbi to include agricultural transformation, quality education, accessible healthcare, youth empowerment, security, local government autonomy and accountable governance. However, he expressed concern over reports of attacks on members of the campaign convoy, destruction of media equipment and the alleged use of tear gas around areas occupied by members of the visiting delegation. He said any involvement of government institutions or security agencies in such incidents would be unacceptable and called for an investigation. Malami also condemned the demolition of the Malami Pressure Group (MPG) headquarters along Sani Abacha Bypass, Birnin Kebbi, describing the circumstances surrounding the incident as troubling. He said the Kebbi State Government’s denial of involvement and its attribution of the demolition to a private ownership dispute did not remove the need for transparency and accountability. According to him, political disagreements should not be used to justify intimidation, destruction of property or the suppression of lawful opposition. Malami said the constitutional rights to freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly must be respected by all levels of government. On the challenges facing Kebbi, he listed banditry, displacement, poverty, food insecurity and disruption of agricultural activities, citing the National Emergency Management Agency’s humanitarian intervention in March 2026 for victims of banditry in Shanga, Yauri and Bunza. He urged the state government to prioritise the protection of farmers, access to education, food affordability and employment opportunities for young people rather than engage in actions capable of intimidating political opponents. item.title: Pope says in ‘fairly good shape’ after lung cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV said Friday he was in “fairly good shape” after lung cancer surgery last month as he began a 12-day tour of South America with a visit to Uruguay. “I know some people were doubtful about this trip taking place,” Leo told reporters on board the papal plane. “I had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward. And I am very happy to say praise the Lord and thanks to wonderful medical assistance, I’m here today, I think in fairly good shape,” he said. Leo, 71, had a cancerous tumor and part of his right lung removed in an operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital on October 13. He was discharged on October 17 and doctors quoted by the Vatican have said he is fit to travel and does not require any further therapy. Asked by reporters if he had advice for people facing a cancer diagnosis, he said: “Not to be afraid. “Early detection is obviously the best way to go and so regular check-ups are a blessing. And take care of yourselves,” he said. Leo was also asked if he had resumed playing tennis — a favorite sport. “Not yet, but I will,” he said. item.title: 2027: Malami’s aide condemns demolition of ADC support group’s office
item.description: A media aide to former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, SAN, has condemned the demolition of the headquarters of the Malami Pressure Group (MPG) in Birnin Kebbi, describing the action as an assault on democratic freedoms and political association. Mohammed Bello Doka, Special Assistant on Media to Malami, alleged that a suspected agency of the Kebbi State Government carried out the demolition on October 30, 2026, a day before the scheduled inauguration of the facility. In a statement dated November 1, Doka said the property belonged to Malami, who had donated it to the MPG, an ADC-affiliated youth support organisation, to serve as its headquarters ahead of the 2027 general elections. He said the facility was demolished without prior communication, formal notice or warning, before it could officially commence operations. Doka described the incident as unacceptable in a constitutional democracy, arguing that it raised concerns about citizens’ rights to own property, associate freely, express political opinions and participate in the democratic process. He questioned the authority behind the demolition, demanding to know which government agency carried out the operation, whether a formal notice was served on the property owner and whether a court order or established administrative procedure authorised the action. He urged the Kebbi State Government to provide a clear explanation of the circumstances surrounding the demolition. Citing the 1999 Constitution, Doka said Sections 39 and 40 guarantee freedom of expression and association, while Sections 43 and 44 provide for property ownership and protection against compulsory acquisition except in accordance with the law. He acknowledged that governments had the authority to enforce planning regulations and building standards but insisted that such powers must be exercised transparently and in accordance with due process. According to him, the timing of the demolition, with the 2027 general elections approaching, raised concerns about the political environment in which opposition parties and their supporters were expected to operate. He argued that democracy required political competition, freedom of association and protection of dissent, adding that citizens should be able to establish political offices and organise meetings without fear of arbitrary interference. Doka also questioned the state’s governance priorities, drawing attention to poverty, malnutrition, food insecurity and insecurity confronting residents of Kebbi. Citing the National Bureau of Statistics’ 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index, he said Kebbi recorded a poverty incidence of 82.2 per cent, compared with the national average of 63 per cent. He further cited the report’s estimate that more than 95 per cent of children under five in the state were multidimensionally poor, representing approximately 820,000 children. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s aide tackles Keyamo over exclusion from ballot
item.description: An aide to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has criticised the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, over his remarks that the heavens would not fall if Atiku was excluded from the 2027 presidential ballot. Ibe, who described Keyamo’s position as an attempt to undermine Nigerians’ democratic rights, said excluding a major political challenger would erode public confidence in the electoral process. He stated this in a Facebook post while reacting to Keyamo’s comments on the possibility of Atiku not participating in the 2027 presidential election. Ibe argued that the exclusion of a major challenger should not be treated as inconsequential, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to decide their preferred presidential candidate through the ballot. “When a ruling party treats the exclusion of a major challenger as inconsequential, it is asking Nigerians to accept that their choice is inconsequential too. That is how you erode public faith in democracy,” he said. Challenging Keyamo, Ibe asked why the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would welcome the prospect of an election without Atiku if it was confident in President Bola Tinubu’s performance. He insisted that Tinubu should be allowed to defend his record before Nigerians, while Atiku should also be given the opportunity to present his case to the electorate. Ibe expressed confidence that Atiku would secure widespread support in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, saying the former vice president’s supporters were prepared to translate their support into votes. “On 16 January 2027, we intend to turn the support Nigerians have shown Atiku into votes and those votes into a mandate. If Nigerians send Tinubu packing at the ballot box, it will be political hell for an APC that has grown accustomed to taking them for granted,” he said. The former vice president’s aide also invoked an Igbo proverb to caution Keyamo and the APC against disregarding the wishes of voters. He quoted the saying, “A gwa ntị okwu, ntị anụghị, e gburu isi, e gburu ya na ntị,” which he translated to mean that when the ear refuses to heed counsel, it shares the fate of the head when it is lost. According to him, a political party that refuses to listen to voters should be prepared for their response on election day. Ibe further vowed that Atiku’s supporters would defend their right to choose their preferred candidate through all lawful means and exercise that right at the polls. He, however, ended his post with a sharp personal attack on Keyamo, saying the minister and his supporters belonged in hell. item.title: Grid ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​​​‍‍‍⁠‌​instability not responsible for IE Band A outage — TCN
item.description: The management of the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) on Friday said grid instability was not responsible for the Ikeja Electric (IE) Band A outage reported by the company on Nov. 3 and Nov. 4. Ms. Ndidi Mba, the General Manager of the Corporate Communication Unit of TCN, disclosed this in a statement in Lagos. According to her, TCN described the attribution as inaccurate and misleading, saying that the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid was not the responsibility of a Distribution Company (DisCo). “By virtue of Section 67 of the Electricity Act 2023, the determination of the root cause of disturbances, shortfalls, and interruptions on the national grid falls exclusively within the defined functions of the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO). “IE, like every other market participant, has no authority to make such determinations, and NISO has made no such attribution of the outages in IE’s notice to TCN,” she said. Mba said that NISO had already explained the situation, attributing the current decline in power generation to gas supply constraints to thermal power stations and reduced output from hydroelectric stations due to lower reservoir inflows. She said that the reduced generation had affected the energy allocated to DisCos, resulting in fewer hours of electricity supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. “The impact on each DisCo varies with available generation and its allocation,” she said. Mba said that the shortfall in electricity supply to IE’s customers was a consequence of reduced generation and the resulting allocation, not any failure of TCN’s transmission network. “TCN can only transmit the energy made available to it and cannot transmit energy that is not generated. “The records for all feeders supplying IE confirm the national picture NISO described. “Of the interruptions recorded on Nov. 1 and 2, 68 percent were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation. “A further 26 percent were due to IE’s non-compliance with load allocation by the National Control Centre (NCC) of NISO or to faults and works on IKEDC’s own network. “The remaining six percent were TCN planned maintenance, switching, or a line limitation. None of the recorded interruptions was a TCN equipment fault or trip,” she said. According to her, the feeders listed in IE’s notice also did not support the company’s claim. “Of the 46 interruptions recorded on the 33kV feeders named in the notice, 29 were frequency-control load shedding arising from low generation, while 14 were recorded against IKEDC. “Nine were for non-compliance with load allocation, and five for faults or trips on its own network. item.title: ‘It’ll Never Be Forgotten’, Flamingos Captain On Hopes Of Winning U-17 World Cup
item.description: Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team captain, Harmony Chidi, says winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup would be an unforgettable moment for her, her teammates, the coaching crew and the country. Speaking to FIFA ahead of the final against Japan in Morocco, Chidi described reaching the last stage of the competition as a significant achievement but said lifting the trophy would make the occasion even more special. “I think it would be a great thing, a joy, and would never be forgotten in life,” she said. “Reaching the final is a very big thing, it’s a great thing and it’s something that we have dreamed of. Winning would be something myself, my country, my team-mates, our coaches, and everybody would be proud of.” The Flamingos have made history by becoming the first African team to reach the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, setting up a title clash with Japan. Their journey to the final followed a difficult start, having lost 2-1 to Poland in their opening Group B match. They recovered to win five consecutive games against Puerto Rico, two-time reigning champions DPR Korea, Mexico, Venezuela and Brazil. Their 3-1 victory over Brazil in the semi-final secured their place in the final and kept alive Nigeria’s hopes of winning the competition for the first time. Head coach Akeem Busari said the team’s response to the opening defeat was driven by psychological guidance, renewed confidence and a change in the players’ attitude and approach. Flamingos captain Chidi Harmony and coach Akeem Busari in a photoshoot with the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy ahead of the final against Japan. Photo credit: fifa.com “After the first game, we needed to sit them down, psychologically talk to them, talk about our game plan and all we have been doing in the sessions,” he told FIFA. “We needed to change our attitude and character, but because of their age, we just needed to talk to them, to counsel them, and those are the points that make the difference.” Busari acknowledged Japan’s quality, pointing to what he observed in their match against DPR Korea, but said the final would present a different challenge for both teams. “From what we saw against DPR Korea, I think it’s the core of what we should expect more of from the Japanese,” he said. “But it’s a different ballgame because, for both us and them, the game will not be the same. The character, mentality and attitude which you approach every game with, and at every other level too, is what really matters.” The coach, who had declared before the tournament that Nigeria wanted to become champions, credited the players for the team’s progress, describing them as the people who had made the achievement possible. “It would be a plus for Africa, for Nigeria, for my own career as a person, but also for the players as well – they are the gladiators. item.title: Military force alone cannot defeat terrorism – Buratai
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai (retd.), has said that military force alone cannot defeat terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need to address poverty, unemployment, poor governance and other socio-economic factors fuelling insecurity. Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions. The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons. “Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. It can create the conditions for peace, but it cannot by itself build peace. “It can degrade a terrorist group; it cannot alone remove the grievances of poverty, ignorance and manipulation from which such groups recruit,” he said. Buratai emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and community participation in counter-insurgency operations, describing local communities as indispensable partners in the fight against terrorism. According to him, security agencies cannot achieve meaningful results without the confidence and cooperation of the communities they are deployed to protect. “No amount of firepower can compensate for poor intelligence. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated. He also warned that human rights violations during military operations could alienate local communities and provide terrorist organisations with propaganda materials to attract new recruits. Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms. He called for stronger counter-terrorism capacity within the Nigeria Police Force, arguing that the military should not continue to shoulder responsibilities traditionally assigned to civilian security institutions. “The military is not the police; it is not the social welfare agency; it is not the school system. When the military is deployed to perform tasks that belong to civil authorities, it becomes overstretched, and the roots of the conflict remain untouched,” he said. item.title: The Obidient Pulse: Obi Warns Against Uncertainty As Opposition Groups Face A Test Of Unity
item.description: A court ruling that has thrown the African Democratic Congress into fresh uncertainty has prompted Peter Obi to warn about the consequences for opposition politics, while disagreements continue among groups supporting his own 2027 bid. Obi reacts to court ruling affecting ADC The Federal High Court in Abuja has nullified the leadership of the African Democratic Congress under Senator David Mark and set aside the party’s processes, including the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as its presidential candidate. The ADC says it will appeal. Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, described the ruling as “unsettling and surprising”. He said there should be certainty about parties and candidates ahead of an election and called for opposition politics to be protected. Obi also accused the ruling APC of engineering the instability, an allegation the party rejected. The court decision concerns the ADC; it does not directly affect Obi’s NDC candidacy. Court fight places opposition unity under pressure The ADC has rejected the judgment and says it will challenge it in court. Atiku has also said he will appeal and seek a stay of execution. The case now puts the spotlight on the judiciary’s role in resolving internal party disputes and on whether opposition parties can maintain stable platforms as the election approaches. Disagreement among Obi’s support groups continues The court ruling comes amid public friction between the OK Movement and leaders of the Obidient Movement and NDC campaign. The OK Movement accused them of fuelling divisions; the NDC campaign dismissed the dispute as a distraction, while the Obidient coordinator’s aide said he was focused on mobilising support for Obi. The exchanges raise a practical question for the campaign: can its different support groups coordinate their work, clarify who speaks for whom and build lasting grassroots organisation? The public disagreements are a reminder that a broad support base needs clear roles and disciplined coordination to turn enthusiasm into effective political mobilisation. The task ahead For the Obidient Movement, the immediate challenge is to keep attention on voters, organisation and the issues facing Nigerians. The movement’s strength will be measured not only by the size of its support, but by how effectively it organises that support across communities and sustains a credible campaign. In a political season increasingly shaped by court cases and internal disputes, the demand from supporters is likely to be simple: less public quarrelling, clearer communication and visible work on the ground.
